extracted.intended_audience: pharmaceutical applicants, sponsors, and regulatory counsel submitting NDAs, ANDAs, or 505(b)(2) applications to FDA
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedures governing meetings, dispute resolution, approval criteria and timing, patent- and exclusivity-related approval delays, foreign data acceptance, complete response letters, and applicant obligations for NDAs, ANDAs, and 505(b)(2) applications submitted to FDA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meetings after complete response
rubrics_metrics.description: At the conclusion of FDA's review of an NDA as designated by the issuance of a complete response letter, FDA will provide the applicant with an opportunity to meet with agency reviewing officials to discuss what further steps need to be taken by the applicant before the application can be approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for such meetings must be directed to the director of the division responsible for reviewing the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other meetings during review
rubrics_metrics.description: Other meetings between FDA and applicants may be held, with advance notice, to discuss scientific, medical, and other issues that arise during the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests shall be directed to the director of the reviewing division. FDA will attempt to grant requests involving important issues and that can be scheduled at mutually convenient times. Unannounced "drop-in" visits are discouraged except for urgent matters (e.g., important new safety issue).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispute resolution — general commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA is committed to resolving differences between applicants and FDA reviewing divisions with respect to technical requirements for applications or abbreviated applications as quickly and amicably as possible through the cooperative exchange of information and views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative/procedural disputes — escalation path
rubrics_metrics.description: When administrative or procedural disputes arise, the applicant should first attempt to resolve the matter with the reviewing division, beginning with the consumer safety officer assigned to the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If resolution is not achieved, the applicant may raise the matter with the ombudsman, whose function is to investigate and facilitate a timely and equitable resolution. Appropriate issues for the ombudsman include difficulties in scheduling meetings, obtaining timely replies, and obtaining timely completion of pending reviews. Further details are in a staff manual guide available under FDA public information regulations (part 20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific and medical disputes — conferences as forum
rubrics_metrics.description: Major scientific issues are ordinarily communicated in a complete response letter; the "end-of-review conference" (§314.102(d)) and the "ninety-day conference" (§314.102(c)) provide timely forums for discussing and resolving scientific and medical issues on which the applicant disagrees with the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific and medical disputes — escalation sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: When scientific or medical disputes arise at other times, applicants should discuss the matter directly with responsible reviewing officials and, if necessary, request meetings with management representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinarily meetings are held first with the Division Director, then with the Office Director, and finally with the Center Director if unresolved. Requests should be directed to the division director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of outside experts in dispute resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: In requesting a meeting to resolve a scientific or medical dispute, applicants may suggest that FDA seek advice of outside experts; FDA may invite advisory committee members or other consultants and applicants may bring their own consultants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For major unresolved scientific/medical policy issues, FDA may refer the matter to a standing advisory committee for consideration and recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drugs with potential for abuse — DEA notification
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will inform the Drug Enforcement Administration under section 201(f) of the Controlled Substances Act when an application or abbreviated application is submitted for a drug that appears to have an abuse potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval decision rule for NDA/ANDA
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will approve an NDA (or ANDA) and send the applicant an approval letter if none of the reasons in §314.125 (or §314.127 for ANDAs) for refusing to approve applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If statutory or exclusivity constraints prevent approval despite meeting requirements, FDA will issue a tentative approval letter. A tentatively approved product is not an approved drug and cannot be marketed until full approval is issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tentative approval circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will issue a tentative approval letter if an application otherwise meets requirements for approval but cannot be approved because of exclusivity or other statutory timing limits (e.g., 7‑year orphan exclusivity, pediatric exclusivity, other exclusivity provisions, or conditions in §314.107(b)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tentative approval is based on information available at the time and is subject to change if new information arises; tentative approval does not permit marketing until full approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval conditioned on draft labeling minor deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will approve an NDA and issue an approval letter on the basis of draft labeling if the only deficiencies concern editorial or similar minor deficiencies in draft labeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such approval is conditioned on the applicant incorporating specified labeling changes exactly as directed and submitting a copy of the final printed labeling prior to marketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory standards and FDA scientific judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will approve an NDA after it determines that the drug meets statutory standards for safety and effectiveness, manufacturing and controls, and labeling; ANDAs after determining manufacturing/controls, labeling, and, where applicable, bioequivalence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of diversity among drugs, FDA exercises scientific judgment to determine the kind and quantity of data required for a particular drug. FDA issues guidance documents, recommendations, and policy statements to communicate views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of foreign data as sole basis — criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: An application based solely on foreign clinical data meeting U.S. criteria may be approved if: (1) the foreign data are applicable to the U.S. population and U.S. medical practice; (2) studies performed by investigators of recognized competence; and (3) data may be considered valid without on‑site inspection or FDA is able to validate via inspection or other appropriate means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to meet any criterion renders the application not approvable on foreign data alone. FDA applies the policy flexibly according to the drug and data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presubmission meetings when relying on foreign data
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are encouraged to meet with agency officials in a "presubmission" meeting when approval based solely on foreign data will be sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of approval defined
rubrics_metrics.description: A 505(b)(2) application or ANDA for a drug product is approved on the date FDA issues an approval letter under §314.105 for the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of patents on approval timing — patent certification outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The status of patents listed for the referenced listed drug must be considered in determining the first possible date on which a 505(b)(2) application or ANDA can be approved; specific patent certifications or statements under §314.50(i) / §314.94(a)(12) affect timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant certifies (A) patent information not submitted, (B) patent expired, (C) patent invalid/unenforceable/not infringed (subject to paragraph IV litigation timing), or (D) no relevant patents, approval may be immediate if no other refusal/delay reasons apply. Method‑of‑use statements and paragraph IV interactions have special rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent information filed after submission — applicant obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the NDA holder files patent information after submission, the 505(b)(2) or ANDA applicant must comply with requirements regarding submission of an appropriate patent certification or statement under §314.50(i)(4),(6) and §314.94(a)(12)(vi),(viii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant submits an amendment certifying patent invalidity/unenforceability/noninfringement and complies with §314.52 or §314.95, the application may be approved immediately upon submission of documentation of receipt of notice of paragraph IV certification; the 45‑day period does not apply in these circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of patent litigation — 30‑month and 7½‑year rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent owner brings suit for patent infringement within 45 days of notice of paragraph IV certification, approval of the 505(b)(2) or ANDA may be approved 30 months after the later of the date of receipt of the notice by any owner or by the NDA holder, unless court extends/reduces the period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rule: if the patented drug product qualifies for 5 years of exclusivity and suit is brought during a specified 1‑year window, approval may be at expiration of 7½ years from approval of the NDA for the patented drug. Courts may alter timing by judgments, injunctions, settlements, mandates, or orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court decisions and appeals affecting approval timing
rubrics_metrics.description: District court decisions of invalidity/unenforceability/non‑infringement may permit approval on the date of judgment or settlement order; appeals and appellate mandates likewise affect approval dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If district court finds infringement and judgment is appealed, approval may occur on issuance of appellate mandate entering judgment for invalidity/unenforceability/non‑infringement; if judgment affirmed or not appealed, approval may be no earlier than date specified by district court under 35 U.S.C. 271(e)(4)(A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary injunctions and their effects
rubrics_metrics.description: If a district court grants a preliminary injunction prohibiting commercial manufacture/sale pending patent issues, and later decides patent invalid/unenforceable/not infringed, approval may follow as provided for court decisions; if patent found infringed, approval timing follows infringement judgment provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of preliminary injunctions and subsequent orders lifting injunctions must be submitted to FDA as part of notification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written consent and court orders permitting earlier approval
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner or exclusive licensee agrees in writing that the 505(b)(2) application or ANDA may be approved any time on or after the date of consent, approval may be granted on or after that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a court order terminates the 30‑month or 7½‑year period, approval may be granted in accordance with the court's order. Dismissals without a finding of infringement allow approval on or after date of order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of approval to tentative approval
rubrics_metrics.description: If FDA issues an approval letter in error or a court enters an order requiring that the date of approval be delayed, FDA will convert the approval to a tentative approval if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tentative approval is distinct from full approval and does not permit marketing until full approval is issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of approval of subsequent ANDAs and 180‑day exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: If an ANDA contains a paragraph IV certification and is not that of a first applicant, it is regarded as a subsequent applicant and will not be approved during periods when any first applicant is eligible for 180‑day exclusivity or during the 180‑day exclusivity period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any applicable 180‑day exclusivity cannot extend beyond the expiration of the patent on which it was based. A first applicant must notify FDA within 30 days of first commercial marketing; failure to notify results in deemed date of first commercial marketing being the approval date. If FDA concludes a first applicant is not actively pursuing approval, FDA may immediately approve subsequent ANDAs if otherwise eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delays due to statutory exclusivity provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will delay approval of a 505(b)(2) application or ANDA if delay is required by exclusivity provisions in §314.108, section 527 (and §316.31), section 505A, or section 505E of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When delayed under these provisions, the application will be approved on the latest of the days specified under the applicable statutes and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirements for court actions and consents
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must submit to FDA copies of judgments, settlement orders, consent decrees, notices of appeals, court orders terminating periods, written consents to approval, preliminary injunctions and subsequent lifting orders, and court orders under 35 U.S.C. 271(e)(4)(A), as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All required information must be sent to the applicant's NDA or ANDA, as appropriate, within 14 days of the date of entry by the court, the date of appeal or expiration of time for appeal, or the date of written consent to approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: 45‑day period after receipt of notice of paragraph IV certification — computation
rubrics_metrics.description: The 45‑day clock for each recipient required to receive notice of paragraph IV certification begins the day after the date of receipt of the applicant's notice; if the 45th day falls on Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday, the 45th day is the next non‑weekend/non‑holiday day.

rubrics_metrics.name: 45‑day period — notification of filing of legal action to FDA
rubrics_metrics.description: The 505(b)(2) or ANDA applicant must notify FDA in writing within 14 days of filing any legal action filed within 45 days of receipt of the notice of paragraph IV certification by any recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification must include: the application number; applicant name; established name of drug or active ingredients/strength/dosage form if no established name; a statement that an action for patent infringement (identified by court, case number, and patent number(s)) has been filed on a specified date. Patent owners or NDA holders may also notify FDA. If no written notification is received before expiration of the 45‑day period or completion of Agency review, the application may be approved upon expiration of the 45‑day period (if applicant confirms no legal action) or upon completion of Agency review, whichever is later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of 45‑day opportunity to file suit
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner or NDA holder (or exclusive licensee) waives its opportunity to file suit within 45 days and submits a valid waiver to FDA before the 45 days elapse, the 505(b)(2) application or ANDA may be approved upon completion of Agency review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA will only accept a waiver in the specific form provided (text specifying receipt of notice, identity of applicant and drug, statement of not intending to file suit before the 45 days elapse, and waiver of opportunity provided by statute).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions relevant to exclusivity and submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions used in exclusivity sections include: 'Approved under section 505(b)', 'Bioavailability study', 'Clinical investigation', 'Conducted or sponsored by the applicant' (including 'substantial support' test), 'Essential to approval', 'New chemical entity', and 'New clinical investigation'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key points: to show 'conducted or sponsored' applicant must be named sponsor on Form FDA‑1571 or provide substantial support (certified CPA statement that applicant provided ≥50% of study cost or explanation); predecessor in interest defined; purchase of nonexclusive rights after completion is insufficient; 'new clinical investigation' excludes bioavailability studies and duplicates of investigations previously relied upon by FDA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete response letter — purpose and content
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will send a complete response letter when it determines it will not approve the application in its present form for reasons given in §314.125/127. A complete response letter will describe all specific deficiencies identified (except as stated in paragraph (a)(3) of the section) and reflect FDA's complete review of data submitted and any amendments reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The letter will identify any amendments not yet reviewed. If FDA determines submitted data are inadequate, it might issue a complete response letter without first conducting required inspections and/or reviewing proposed labeling. When possible, the letter will recommend actions the applicant might take to place the application in condition for approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant actions after complete response letter
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving a complete response letter, the applicant must: (1) resubmit the application addressing all deficiencies; (2) withdraw the application; or (3) request an opportunity for a hearing on whether there are grounds for denial under section 505(d) or (j)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resubmissions are classified: Class 1 resubmission = new 2‑month review cycle; Class 2 = new 6‑month review cycle. Resubmissions of NDA supplements other than efficacy supplements start a new review cycle the same length as the initial cycle; major resubmission of an abbreviated application = new 6‑month cycle; minor resubmission of an abbreviated application = new review cycle appropriate to the submission. Requests for hearings must be submitted to the Associate Director for Policy, CDER; FDA will act within 60 days (or agreed different period) to approve the application or refuse and give written notice of opportunity for a hearing under §314.200 and statutory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to act after complete response letter — withdrawal and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant agrees to extend the review period under section 505(c)(1) or (j)(5)(A) until it takes one of the actions listed. FDA may consider an applicant's failure to take such actions within 1 year after issuance of a complete response letter to be a request to withdraw the application, unless the applicant has requested an extension of time to resubmit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA will grant any reasonable extension request. If FDA considers the failure to be a withdrawal request, the agency will notify the applicant in writing; the applicant will have 30 days from notification to explain why the application should not be withdrawn and to request an extension of time to resubmit.
